name: poker-odds
title: Poker odds
description: Winning and improvement chances for teaching and display: what a hand can still become with the exact chance, the chance of holding the best hand against opponents, and Chen's starting score.

text.purpose: Answers three questions about a player's two hole cards and the board. `rows`: what the hand is now and every better hand it can still become, each with the exact chance that the cards it needs arrive by the river, in the order a learner reads them (a straight low to high, pairs grouped, kickers last); counted exactly from the flop on and from a fixed sample of boards before it, and cached. `winChance`: the chance of holding the best hand at the river against some opponents, by simulation, where each opponent can be assumed to hold at least a given starting score (a raiser is not on a random hand). `startingScore`: Chen's pre-flop score. `shownCards`: a shown hand's combination in reading order with the kickers asked for.
text.userInputs: The installer collects two optional integers:
text.integration: Create it with `createOdds(ranking, settings)`, passing the hand-ranking interface (poker-hand-ranking) which carries the card codes and deck of the connected card-deck. A table shows `rows` to a player who asked for odds; poker-strategy calls `winChance` and `startingScore`; a replay screen calls `shownCards`. TypeScript only: the Swift and Kotlin apps display rows the server sends, they do not compute them.
text.infrastructure: No deployed service, account or key. CPU only: exact counting for river and turn is a few milliseconds; the pre-flop sample of 2000 boards takes a few tens of milliseconds on this machine, then is served from the cache.
text.verification: `node --test tests/server.test.ts` checks river, flop and pre-flop rows, the exact flush-draw probability against the closed form, `chance` against enumeration of every board that can follow, straight-flush and flush cases, the cache and its size setting, Chen's scores, known matchups within sampling error (aces against a random hand about 85 percent) and the effect of opponent ranges. The extraction was compared with the recipe's odds.ts and bot.ts equity on 60 random spots: rows, scores and win chances identical.
text.scenarios: A learner taps 'my chances' on the flop and sees a flush at 35 percent and a pair at 100. A coach shows the chance of winning against three opponents before the flop. A computer player prices a call.
text.updates: The seeded pre-flop sample determines the pre-flop rows. Removing the component removes the files; nothing is stored.

agentInstructions: Select this component when the application teaches or displays hand chances, and always when poker-strategy is selected. Connect its hand-ranking input to poker-hand-ranking and its card-deck input to the application's card-deck. Leave the settings at their defaults unless the pre-flop rows are too slow or too coarse.
developerInstructions: No accounts or keys. `sampleBoards` (default 2000) is the number of pre-flop boards sampled for the rows; more is smoother and slower. `cacheSize` (default 500) is how many card sets are remembered. Call `createOdds(handRanking)` once and reuse it.

suitability.notes: Pure library, CPU only. No hosted service, account or provider limit applies; the cost per call is milliseconds (exact turn and river) to tens of milliseconds (pre-flop sample), measured informally on the build machine only.
